ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, individual and corporate general partners, directors, senior officers and authorized signatories against: (1) FINTRAC guidance and PCMLTFA reporting requirements; (2) the Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (3) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (4) OFAC SDN List (U.S.); (5) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists where international nexus exists; (6) open-source adverse media and law enforcement alerts. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any person identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) as defined by FATF, a domestic PEP, or a person connected to a PEP; EDD includes source of wealth and source of funds verification. Results must be documented and retained for five years after the date the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and NUANS Name Search and Reservation Portal (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada); for provincial extra-provincial registration of limited partnerships, the applicable provincial registry, e.g., ServiceOntario Business Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate name requirements permit names in English, French, or both official languages. Names must be in Latin script; transliteration from non-Latin scripts is not permitted for the computerized name system. The name must include a distinctive element and a legal element such as 'Limited', 'Limitée', 'L.P.', 'S.E.C.', or 'Limited Partnership'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing federal or provincial name, and must not imply a connection with the Crown, government, royal family, or a regulated profession or activity except with prior consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: FOUNDATION (where implying charitable or non-profit status)
CLINIC (unless the entity holds the necessary medical facility license)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name refusal, the applicant may file a written appeal within 30 days of the refusal notice to the Director of Corporations Canada (or the provincial registry director for provincial LPs) under the applicable business corporations or limited partnership act. The appeal submission must specify the distinctiveness of the proposed name, include legal arguments distinguishing it from conflicting names, and provide supporting consents or letters from the conflicting name holder, if obtained. The Director will issue a reconsideration decision within 30 days after receipt. A further appeal to the Federal Court of Canada may be commenced under section 18 of the Federal Courts Act (or judicial review of the provincial tribunal decision) if the Director or provincial registry affirms the refusal. Extension requests must be filed before the expiry of the initial reservation window and are generally granted for a further 90 days in writing, subject to continued availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only as a mailing address and for service of process for the limited partnership's registered office, but it is not acceptable as the principal place of business, manufacturing facility, laboratory, storage site, or the physical establishment address required for Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL). For this IVD manufacturing scope, the commercial substance requirement mandates a fixed physical address with appropriate laboratory/manufacturing premises. A virtual office purporting to serve as the manufacturing facility will result in denial of the MDEL application and may trigger anti-avoidance review by the Canada Revenue Agency regarding GST/HST and income tax registrations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is high: 75% likelihood of a Health Canada on-site MDEL compliance inspection within the first 18 months after licence issuance; 40% likelihood of an unannounced re-inspection in any subsequent year for GMP compliance; 30-45% likelihood of a Canada Revenue Agency field audit of GST/HST and commercial substance indicators during the first three years of operation.

Reg. 490/91 (LP registration); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 5 (federal incorporation of corporate General Partner); Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (partnership pass-through taxation)

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed by the Limited Partnership Agreement. Escrow account not mandated by statute; however, segregated partnership operating funds and a dedicated Canadian bank account are required to preserve limited liability and to obtain the CRA Business Number.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Limited Partnership accepts the subscription for the partnership interest as set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement and records the initial capital contribution; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at the address described in the formation documents, and that the statutory declaration is filed with the provincial registry; FURTHER RESOLVED, that Jane Doe is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and Managing Partner, and John Roe as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual meeting; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute all registrations, open financial institution accounts, and conduct all statutory filings necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) and accredited NUANS search houses
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed limited partnership name and obtain a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report dated within the last 90 days. Verify that the name is not confusingly similar to any existing federal or provincial entity, and confirm the availability of the proposed corporate General Partner name for CBCA incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and business description
Identification documents for the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a confusing similarity is flagged, file a written rebuttal with a consent letter from the conflicting name holder, or adopt a revised distinctive name and submit a new NUANS search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Statutory Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel; Commissioner of Oaths or Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement, including capital contribution schedules, distribution waterfall, and management authority of the General Partner. Have the partners execute Form 1 - Declaration of Limited Partnership before a commissioner of oaths or notary public, ensuring witness signatures are completed in accordance with provincial practice.
required_dossiers: General Partner board resolution approving the partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected as incomplete, correct the omissions, re-execute before the notary, and refile with the registry; no additional government fee applies if corrected within the standard processing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Registration of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (OnCorp / online registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 - Declaration of Limited Partnership together with the NUANS report and pay the prescribed registration fee by wire or credit card. Upon issuance of the registration certificate, verify the Ontario Limited Partnership Number and note any requirement for extra-provincial registration in other Canadian provinces where business will be conducted.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration of the corporate General Partner (if already incorporated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit an administrative correction or refile the declaration with the registry. For urgent transactions, pay the expedited service fee to secure same-week processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Incorporation of the Corporate General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Articles of Incorporation for a federal unlimited liability corporation or a regular federal corporation to act as the corporate General Partner under the Canada Business Corporations Act. Designate the initial registered office and first board of directors, file the consent of directors, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form 3 - Initial Registered Office and First Board of Directors
Consent to act as director forms
NUANS report for the General Partner name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are rejected for non-compliance, amend the filings and refile online. If the NUANS report has expired, obtain a new report; a certificate already issued may only be corrected by Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Limited Partnership for a Business Number through the CRA Business Registration Online service. Apply for the GST/HST program account (RT), payroll deductions account (RP), and the Canada Border Services Agency import/export account (RM) for IVD instrument and cartridge cross-border trade. Confirm that the partnership will be taxed on a pass-through basis under section 96 of the Income Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation of the General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA issues a notice of deficiency, respond in My Business Account with the missing partnership records and request issuance of the BN confirmation letter. GST/HST account elections that are incorrect may be corrected using Form GST-ACC.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portals: Business Registration Online (BRO) at www.canada.ca/business-registration and My Business Account at www.canada.ca/my-cra-business-account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident limited partnership carrying on business or establishing a permanent establishment in Canada must apply to CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 or the Business Registration Online service. The application requires legal entity details (limited partnership agreement, provincial/territorial partnership registration, if any), proof of Canadian place of business or appointment of a Canadian representative for service, and selection of program accounts: GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), import/export account (RM). No statutory requirement for a Canadian resident agent at the federal registration stage, but CRA requires a Canadian address or authorized representative where a non-resident has no Canadian presence. Upon approval, CRA issues a 9-digit BN and program account numbers. The LP must also consider provincial partnership registration and registration for provincial PST/QST where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (s. 96). Income, gains, losses and credits are allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level. Non-resident partners are subject to Canadian Part I tax on Canadian-source business income attributable to the partnership; a non-resident limited partner may also be exposed to Part XIII withholding on partnership distributions characterized as dividends, interest, rents, or royalties. Canada taxes on a residence/territorial basis: Canadian-source income of the partnership is taxable in Canada; foreign-source income may remain taxable in Canada if treaty protection is unavailable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box election comparable to the U.S. rules; LP transparency is mandatory rather than elective. A partnership may elect out of the default partnership fiscal period (ITA s. 96(3)) to align with calendar year. A non-resident partner may file a s. 216 Canadian income tax return election for rental and timber investment income, but this is not available for active manufacturing/trading income. For cross-border U.S. classification purposes, the Canadian LP can be classified as a partnership or disregarded entity through U.S. IRS Form 8832 elections, but such elections have no effect on Canadian federal status. Under the new Canadian hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 18.2, 18.3, 20.2), no affirmative election is provided; deductibility/non-deductibility adjustments are mandatory if hybrid mismatch outcomes exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); a federal VAT imposed at 5% (GST) plus provincial harmonized increases of 8% or 10% in participating provinces (HST at 13% or 15% respectively).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide gross revenue from 'taxable supplies' (including zero-rated supplies) in the current or immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, mandatory registration unless the supplier qualifies as a small supplier. For non-residents carrying on business in Canada, the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies, except that making taxable supplies in Canada alone does not automatically require registration where the threshold is not met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no federal real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing clearance platform, or digital stamping requirement. Registered suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST information (ETA s. 169(4) and s. 221(2)). Registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million must file GST/HST returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or GST/HST TELEFILE. Large registers are subject to CRA electronic payment and remittance requirements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia: Zero-rating for exported tangible personal property is available under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act where the supplier properly exports the goods 'directly outside Canada' within prescribed conditions: goods shipped by the supplier or transferred to a carrier for export, with proof of export required. Supplies of services made to non-residents are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V (s. 7 and s. 9) where the service is performed for a non-resident and the recipient's benefit is received outside Canada; services rendered in respect of exported goods may also be zero-rated. For IVD equipment and microfluidic cartridges manufacturing, exports of finished medical diagnostic devices qualify as zero-rated supplies upon compliance with documentary evidence requirements. The exporter must maintain records establishing the exporting transaction, including foreign destination and physical movement, for six years as required by CRA record-keeping rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or CBSA electronic export report/ACI eManifest)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Commercial Sales Invoice with full product details
Foreign customs entry or destination customs document
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT wire transfer evidence
Proof of title transfer and shipping risk (e.g., Incoterms, export contract)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: For exported goods, CRA will reassess a zero-rated transaction at the standard 5% GST/HST rate if the supplier cannot substantiate physical export under CRA policy P-208 (Sufficient Evidence in Respect of Exported Goods and Services) within the normal four-year reassessment period (three years for most corporations, extended indefinitely where misrepresentation or neglect). Clawback may include GST/HST in addition to interest, and the exporter may lose input tax credits previously claimed on export-related inputs. Civil penalties under ETA s. 285.1 impose 15% of the tax amount for deliberate false statements or omission made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence. Criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 327 may result in fines, imprisonment and mandatory restitution; for fraudulent export zero-rating involving false customs declarations, CBSA and CRA may jointly prosecute.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) - monetary policy, currency issuance and lender of last resort, holding no exchange-control powers. Prudential supervision of Schedule I banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46). AML/CTF and cross-border EFT surveillance rest with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17). Foreign-investment screening that brackets banking permissions rests with the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry under the Investment Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 28 (1st Supp.)).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility with no exchange-control regime. Canada abolished the Foreign Exchange Control Board in 1951 and operates a free-floating CAD; neither the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) nor the Bank of Canada Act imposes convertibility restrictions, repatriation approvals, conversion ratios, or prior licensing for capital contributions, dividends, royalties, intercompany loans or profit remittances. The Bank of Canada does not target the exchange rate and intervenes only in exceptional disorderly-market circumstances. Remaining frictions are: (i) FINTRAC EFT reporting for cross-border wires at or above CAD 10,000 (filed by the bank, not the LP); (ii) Investment Canada Act review only when a non-Canadian acquires control of a Canadian business above annually-adjusted WTO thresholds (approximately CAD 1.3-1.4 billion for 2024-2025); and (iii) LP pass-through taxation - non-resident limited partners are statutorily deemed to carry on business through the partnership's Canadian permanent establishment under ITA s. 96(4), leaving their share of Canadian-source IVD manufacturing profits taxable on a net basis under Part I with treaty mechanics, but with no quantitative limit on remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender ratio, no repatriation deadline and no requirement to convert export proceeds into CAD for IVD or medical-device exporters. The LP may hold USD and EUR receipts indefinitely in domestic foreign-currency accounts or in offshore correspondent accounts. Side obligations are limited to: (i) correct accrual of export revenue and inventory under ITA ss. 9 and 12; (ii) filing Form T106 for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with non-residents; and (iii) bank-side FINTRAC EFT reporting for wires at or above CAD 10,000. No currency-surrender declaration, export-proceeds certificate or Bank of Canada approval is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. Offshore fintech EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud or US-chartered neobanks) may operate in Canada only as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses (MSBs); they cannot take deposits under the Bank Act's unauthorized deposit-taking restrictions, are not CDIC-insured, and cannot issue documentary letters of credit required by this entity's import-heavy trade payables. Legal use is limited to collecting small distributor prepayments, paying suppliers below CAD 25,000, and expense disbursements, provided the EMI is FINTRAC-registered and does not hold itself out as a 'bank' in Canada. The primary banking estate must remain with a Schedule I bank; an EMI may be added only as a secondary collection node with the relationship banker's written consent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person mandate with a narrow remote exception. Canada does not statutorily prohibit remote onboarding, but Schedule I banks will require, for this Medium-Risk-Enhanced profile: (i) the General Partner's authorized officer (director or CFO) to attend an in-person KYC/UBO interview at a Canadian branch and execute the wet-signature account mandate, including dual-signatory authority for LC issuance; (ii) if no Canadian-resident officer exists, a Canadian-licensed lawyer must present a notarized Corporate Power of Attorney, certified copies of the LP agreement and the beneficial-ownership register; and (iii) the LP must evidence a physical registered office and operating address (lease or utility bill). The Canada 'federal' scope is achieved through the CRA Business Number, a provincially-registered LP with extra-provincial registrations, and a CBCA (or provincial) incorporation of the General Partner. Remote video onboarding is accepted only for low-risk clients or where the bank already holds an active relationship with the General Partner's principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding 25% or more of capital obscure UBO traceability under FINTRAC's 25% beneficial-ownership control rule.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Beneficial Ownership Register naming every individual with 25% or more ownership or control; passport and ID copies; provincial certificate of Limited Partnership plus extra-provincial registration; notarized source-of-wealth letter from an independent accountant for each non-resident partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office at a virtual or corporate-agent address with no demonstrable Canadian operating footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed 12-month lease or warehouse sublease for the Canadian IVD site; current utility bill; Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL, SOR/98-282) naming the LP's Canadian address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutorily-regulated IVD and medical-device industry without Canadian and US licensing, raising unlawful-health-product flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Health Canada MDEL; ISO 13485:2016 Quality Management System certificate; FDA establishment registration and product listing for US point-of-care analyzers; Class II/III Medical Device Licence evidence if any product is sold in Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags on Asian procurement corridors (microfluidic resins, injection molds, fine chemicals).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-packaged trade file: pro-forma invoices; vendor corporate registration certificates; HS 9018/9027 classifications aligned to NAICS 334516; executed supply contracts under Incoterms 2020; third-party screening for sanctioned counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction wires into the Capital Escrow Account from tax-haven or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreements and capital-account statements; independent accountant's source-of-funds letter; sanctions screening confirmation under the United Nations Act and OSFI guidance; declaration that funds are not derived from proceeds of crime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; for a December 31 fiscal period end, no later than June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA may impose a late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per partner, up to CAD 2,500 per return, plus prescribed interest; continued non-filing may lead to an administrative demand, additional penalties, and prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partner Information Slips and Allocation Schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); copies must be provided to each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the calendar year in which the partnership fiscal period ended
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate information slips are subject to CRA penalties of CAD 25 per day per partner up to CAD 2,500, plus gross-negligence penalties in cases of knowing understatement or omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual GST/HST filers, within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year fiscal period, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file timely may trigger a penalty of 5% of the unremitted amount plus 1% per full month of default, up to 12 months, together with daily compounded prescribed-rate interest and CRA collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and UBO Confirmation Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Partnership records; available for CRA inspection and provincial registry verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than 6 months after the fiscal period end, before the T5013 filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete register or UBO documentation may result in CRA administrative penalties for inaccurate allocation records and may expose a limited partner to loss of limited-liability protection under provincial limited partnership legislation if control participation is not properly documented.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No federal statutory audit is imposed solely on a limited partnership. A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the partnership agreement requires audited financial statements, the LP is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, the LP is designated by CRA as a large partnership for audit verification, or a lender or financing covenant requires certified statements. Private LPs below these triggers may prepare compiled or reviewed financial statements instead.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for publicly accountable enterprises and large designated entities; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS for private limited partnerships at the partners' election, in accordance with the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Canada does not maintain a federal UBO registry for limited partnerships. Annually, the general partner must confirm each limited partner's identity, ownership percentage, contribution balance, and ultimate beneficial ownership details from the Register of Partners. Any transfer of a partnership interest must be recorded in the partner register with the effective date and updated percentage, and the resulting allocation must be reported on the T5013. This annual confirmation must be completed before the T5013 filing deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200-750 per year, depending on province and scope of registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000-25,000 for a full statutory-quality audit; USD 2,000-6,000 for reviewed or compiled financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate rate; provincial rates apply separately, e.g., Ontario 11.5% for manufacturing)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED investment tax credit (up to 35% for qualifying expenditures); Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) for manufacturing and processing equipment (Class 43.1/43.2); 10% Investment Tax Credit for qualified property

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 – Partnership Information Return (filed via CRA's EFILE or NETFILE for partnerships)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the last day of the 5th month following the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, due May 31)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (loss) from active business carried on in Canada
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report their share of Canadian-source business income; the partnership must allocate income to each partner based on the partnership agreement.
For non-residents, taxable income is subject to Part I tax on Canadian-source income; treaty relief may apply if the partner is a resident of a treaty country.
The partnership must provide each partner with a T5013 slip showing their share; non-residents must file a T1 or T2 return if they have Canadian-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 1% of the partnership's net income (if any) plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, minimum CAD 100. For failure to file information returns, penalties under ITA s.162(1) apply: CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (for non-resident shareholders; reduced under tax treaties, e.g., 5% for substantial shareholding under US/Canada treaty)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident must provide a completed NR-301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) and a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the home country tax authority. The payer must withhold at the treaty rate if the documentation is provided before payment; otherwise, the statutory rate applies and a refund can be claimed via the T1 or T2 return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 10% (e.g., US, UK); Interest: statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 15% (e.g., US, UK) or 10% for arm's length interest under certain treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods transactions, CAD 500,000 for services, and CAD 250,000 for other transactions (per CRA guidance). Additionally, documentation is mandatory if the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds CAD 50 million or assets exceed CAD 10 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the 'substance over form' doctrine. For partnerships, the CRA may scrutinize the economic substance of transactions to ensure they are not artificial or lacking commercial purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful evasion of federal income tax, including false statements, omission of income, or fraudulent deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of the tax evaded (ITA s.163(2)); criminal prosecution under ITA s.239: fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for corporate tax debts under ITA s.160 (for transfers) and s.227.1 (for unremitted withholdings). Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a shell entity to artificially shift profits, avoid tax, or launder money; lack of economic substance in the partnership structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment (ITA s.245) disallowing tax benefits; penalties up to 50% of the tax benefit (ITA s.163(2)); criminal charges under the Criminal Code for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for fraudulent conveyances; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), including inadequate record-keeping, reporting, or compliance program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2 million for individuals and CAD 5 million for entities per violation; criminal penalties for willful non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally liable for AML violations if they knowingly participate or are negligent; fines, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalty of 10% of the adjustment amount (ITA s.247(3)) if documentation is inadequate; interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties if they knowingly participate in transfer pricing mispricing; civil restitution and potential criminal charges for tax evasion.
